  1. **Autosave is a direct re-use of the existing DS-06 coordinator, not a new one.** `NoteContentForm` calls `useAutosaveField<string>` exactly as any other field would, with two Notes-specific tunings layered on top, not inside, the shared hook: a longer debounce (`NOTE_AUTOSAVE_DEBOUNCE_MS = 1500`, vs. DS-06's 800ms short-field default) so continuous typing on a long document coalesces into one save per pause instead of one per keystroke-adjacent field, and a client-side size check (`validateNoteContentSize`, reusing FND-08's `markdownSourceByteLength`/`MARKDOWN_SOURCE_MAX_BYTES` — no second limit) as the hook's `validate`, so an oversized document is refused before a save is even attempted rather than always waiting on a round trip to learn the same thing from the server's authoritative `parseMarkdownSource` boundary, which remains the real limit. The mutate route and its `update_content` intent (NOTES-01A/B) are unchanged — autosave POSTs the identical intent on its own trigger instead of a Save button's click, so there is still exactly one persistence path.
  2. **Notes' Delete/Restore is the generic `EntityRepository.softDelete`/`.restore`, used directly — no second lifecycle column, no Notes-specific deletion model.** The `/notes/:noteId/mutate` route gains `delete`/`restore` intents with their OWN anchor check (`entities.getById(id, { includeDeleted: true })`, since restore must find an already-deleted Note and a repeat delete/restore must stay the idempotent no-op the repository already guarantees) — deliberately separate from `rename`/`update_content`'s existing ACTIVE-only anchor check, which stays unchanged so a deleted Note remains uneditable through its canonical route exactly as before. The kernel-reserved `entity.deleted`/`entity.restored` Activity events (already emitted by the repository) are reused as-is; no new `note.deleted` event is registered.
  3. **Delete is a single click plus a DS-10 Undo toast, not a DS-10b `ConfirmationDialog`.** Soft-delete is fully reversible with no blocking precondition (unlike Projects' archive, which can be genuinely blocked by unfinished tasks and therefore warrants an explanatory confirm step) — DS-10's documented preference is Undo over a confirmation dialog for exactly this shape of action (`FEEDBACK_AND_INSPECTOR.md`, AGENTS.md §7). The click performs the REAL mutation immediately (through the same trusted, workspace-bound route as everything else — never an optimistic-only client state); `onUndo` calls the mirror `restore` intent. The durable, always-available second path back is a plain Active/Deleted `SegmentedFilter` on the Notes collection (promoted from Projects' PROJ-01-local component to `~/shared/segmented-filter`, since it is now used identically by two modules — DESIGN_SYSTEM.md's "add to the ONE shared system, never fork" rule), whose Deleted view lists ONLY soft-deleted Notes and offers Restore per row.
  4. **A minimal, additive kernel extension: `deletedOnly` on `EntityRepository.list`.** The Deleted Notes view needs a bounded, cursor-paginated, "soft-deleted records only" read — the existing `includeDeleted` flag means "active + deleted", not "deleted only", and filtering that client-side would silently break pagination bounds. `ScopedListEntitiesInput.deletedOnly?: boolean` (taking precedence over `includeDeleted`) is a same-shape sibling to the existing flag: its own bound `CursorScope` field (cursor format version bumped 2 → 3) so a cursor from one mode is rejected under another, exactly mirroring how `includeDeleted` was already bound. This is an evolution of the EXISTING generic list contract, not a second listing path.
  5. **A deleted Note's canonical route stays a plain 404 — it is never rendered read-only.** Soft-deleted entities already read as "not found" everywhere in the kernel (`getById` excludes them by default); Notes does not special-case this. Restore is reachable only from the Deleted collection view (or the Undo toast), never from a bespoke "this note is deleted" state on `/notes/:noteId`.
- **Consequences.** *Easy:* autosave correctness (coalescing, staleness, retry, failure-preserves-draft) is inherited for free — no new state machine to design, test or maintain, and DS-06 gains its first full-document-scale consumer, proving the coordinator's value-shape-agnostic design claim in practice; Notes' lifecycle UI is the first generic, reusable template a future module (e.g. People, Meetings) can copy without re-deriving the anchor-check/idempotency/Undo pattern from scratch; the `deletedOnly` list extension is available to any future module needing an honest "Deleted" collection view, not just Notes. *Hard:* two DIFFERENT anchor-check shapes now coexist on the same mutate route (active-only for edit intents, includeDeleted-aware for lifecycle intents) — a future intent added to this route must consciously choose the right one; the offline/failure-attribution UI (`useOnlineStatus`) and the debounce/size-validation tuning are Notes-local for now, not yet promoted to DS-06 defaults, since Notes remains the only full-document autosave consumer. *Accepted:* Delete has no typed-confirmation step (unlike a `DangerousAction` phrase-gate) — acceptable because the action is fully, immediately reversible via two independent paths (Undo toast, Deleted collection), matching the DS-10 Undo-over-confirm precedent rather than Settings' irreversible-action precedent.
- **Alternatives considered.**
  - *A brand-new autosave coordinator tuned for large documents.* Rejected — the existing pure reducer (`~/shared/forms/autosave.ts`) has no dependency on value size or shape; its guarantees hold identically for a 10-character field and a 1 MiB document. Building a second one would be exactly the "second Notes-specific persistence/state model" the brief forbids, for no behavioural gain.
  - *Mirroring Projects' `ProjectSettingsRepository`/`archived_at` pattern for Notes' lifecycle.* Rejected — that is a Project-specific, business-state-driven archive (blockable by unfinished tasks, its own settings table); Notes has no analogous business rule to gate on, and the generic `EntityRepository.softDelete`/`.restore` already exists and is exactly what "delete this record" means for a non-spine entity type. Building a `note_details.deleted_at` column (a second lifecycle column) was also rejected for the same reason FND-02 centralised lifecycle in the first place.
  - *A `ConfirmationDialog`-gated Delete (mirroring Projects' `ArchiveGroup`), with a Settings tab hosting it.* Rejected — Notes has no other capability that would justify a third tab existing at all (`NoteOverview.tsx`'s NOTES-01B comment: "no empty tab for a future capability"), and the action itself has no blocking precondition to explain in a confirmation body, so the added friction would contradict DS-10's own stated preference.
  - *Filtering `entities.list({ includeDeleted: true })` client/route-side down to deleted-only rows for the Deleted view.* Rejected — a page of N rows fetched with `includeDeleted: true` can legitimately contain zero deleted rows, silently breaking the "bounded pagination, truthful counts" requirement; a first-class `deletedOnly` scope keeps the guarantee at the same layer every other list filter already lives in.
  - *A rendered, read-only canonical record view for a deleted Note (e.g. `/notes/:id` shows the content with a "Restore" action inline).* Rejected — every other soft-deleted entity in the kernel already reads as "not found" via the default `getById`; special-casing Notes to render a bespoke deleted-state page would be a second, inconsistent lifecycle presentation for no proven need, when the Deleted collection view already serves the "find and restore it" job.

### ADR-043 — The first-class Tasks module: the four-question planning model, Time Sectors, Someday/Maybe, and derived display-state

- **Status:** Accepted.
- **Context.** Tasks already exist as a real, persistent kernel model: the FND-07 spine owns Task identity, completion and Area/Project parentage; the additive `task_details` slice (ADR-028) owns workflow status, priority, due/scheduled dates and a Markdown description; the accepted Waiting model (ADR-029) owns blocking; planning (ADR-030) treats the scheduled date as the owner's commitment; and the ONE canonical Task Drawer (ADR-028/ADR-033) edits a task identically from Today and Projects. What was missing was a **workspace-wide place to capture, plan and manage** that work — `/tasks` was a placeholder. TASKS-01 builds it. The forces: (1) real planning needs *four separate questions* answered independently, not one overloaded status; (2) the Todoist P1–P4 / Eisenhower vocabulary the owner already thinks in cannot be expressed by the legacy three-value `low/medium/high` priority; (3) Carl Pullein's **Time Sectors** ("when do I intend to work on this?") are a distinct axis from Project parentage ("what body of work is this?") and from the scheduled/due dates; (4) **Someday/Maybe** is a genuine commitment state, not a priority, a hold, a sector or a delete; and (5) none of this may create a second Task identity, Drawer, Activity stream or relationship model.
- **Decision.**
  1. **Four separate dimensions, never collapsed into one status field.** (a) *Why it deserves attention* — Eisenhower **priority P1–P4**. (b) *What to do with it* — the Matrix's Do / Defer / Delegate / Delete-Review actions (a presentation over priority + lifecycle, not a stored field). (c) *When to work on it* — **Time Sector** (planning window), **scheduled date** (owner-calendar day) and **due date** (deadline), three fields that never silently overwrite one another. (d) *Genuine commitment* — **commitment state** Active vs Someday/Maybe.
  2. **Priority becomes canonical P1–P4, reusing the existing field — no second "quadrant" field.** `task_details.priority` is widened from `low/medium/high` to `p1|p2|p3|p4` (`null` = unprioritised, still meaningful — an untriaged task). The canonical mapping is **P1 · Do** (urgent + important), **P2 · Defer** (important, not urgent), **P3 · Delegate** (urgent, lower personal importance), **P4 · Delete / Review** (neither). The Matrix maps priority → quadrant directly; dropping a task into a quadrant sets its priority. P4 is never auto-deleted; its quadrant offers deliberate actions (Keep as P4 · Move to Someday/Maybe · Cancel · Delete). Legacy values are remapped once by migration `0012` (`high→p1`, `medium→p2`, `low→p3`).
  3. **Time Sector is an additive `task_details.time_sector` column**, a closed CHECK set `this_week | next_week | this_month | next_month | long_term | routines` (or `NULL` = **Inbox**, derived, not stored). It answers "when do I intend to address this", independent of the scheduled date (a specific day) and the due date (a deadline); the three coexist (e.g. *due 18 Aug · sector This Week · scheduled Wednesday*). Sector is **not** another Project hierarchy and moving a task between sectors changes only planning intent — never parentage, priority, dates or completion. Sector transitions are always explicit and user-controlled; the system never auto-promotes Next Week → This Week or manufactures commitments. Boundaries use the existing owner-timezone/date infrastructure (`~/shared/datetime`), never ad-hoc browser-local code.
  4. **Someday/Maybe is a first-class `task_details.commitment_state` column** (`active | someday`, default `active`). Someday means "may be worth doing, not currently committed" — distinct from P4, On hold, Waiting, a sector, Cancelled and Deleted. Someday tasks remain real Tasks retaining title/description/Project/Goal/Area/relationships; they are **excluded from active counts, Today, Upcoming, overdue and normal execution views**, carry no warning/guilt indicators, appear in a dedicated Someday/Maybe view, and support Keep / Activate (into a sector) / Delete.
  5. **Workflow status extends minimally.** The persisted open-state vocabulary widens from `todo | in_progress` to `todo | in_progress | on_hold | cancelled` (the existing `task_details.status` column, its CHECK set widened by the migration — the column is not renamed, to keep the change to a value-set widening). **Completed stays spine-derived, Waiting stays waiting-model-derived, Someday/Maybe stays commitment-derived, and Inbox/Planned stay DERIVED** (a task with no sector and no scheduled date reads as Inbox; an active task with a sector or scheduled date reads as Planned) — none of those four are persisted in the status column, so nothing can contradict. Cancelled ≠ Deleted: Cancelled is a deliberate decision not to proceed, retained in history; Deleted is the existing reversible soft-delete lifecycle.
  6. **ONE deterministic display-state precedence, in ONE shared pure evaluator** (`~/shared/task-record/task-view.ts`, consumed by Tasks, Today and Projects — no duplicated status logic): **Deleted → Completed → Cancelled → Waiting → On hold → Someday/Maybe → In progress → Planned → Inbox**. State is always carried by a label, never colour alone.
  7. **Delegation is honest and additive** (`task_details.delegate_to` plain text, plus a delegated date, follow-up date and optional note). People is not yet a module, so the delegatee is free text now; the column is designed so a future Person EntityLink can coexist or replace it without a destructive migration. Choosing Delegate from the Matrix offers to set P3, record the delegatee, enter Waiting through the **existing accepted Waiting mechanism**, and set a follow-up date — but P3 never *requires* a delegatee (the quadrant is the priority; delegation details record whether delegation actually happened).
  8. **A new read-only workspace-wide Tasks projection/repository provides presentation/query ownership only** — it is never a second mutation authority. All mutations continue to flow through the spine (`createTask`, completion, parentage) and the workspace-bound `TaskRepository` (details, waiting, planning, and the new sector/commitment/workflow/delegation writes). Every workspace-wide read is bounded, workspace-scoped, N+1-free, server-authoritatively filtered/sorted, and cursor-paginated with an **opaque, versioned, scope-bound cursor** that binds workspace + view + state + sector + commitment + priority + Project/Goal/Area scope + sort + relevant date window; a cursor that mismatches its query scope is rejected calmly, never reinterpreted.
  9. **Creation from `/tasks` respects spine parentage.** A Task structurally requires exactly one parent — an Area OR a Project (the spine makes "no parent" unrepresentable). `/tasks` creation therefore offers a fast searchable parent selector (Projects primary, Areas permitted), showing Area/Goal context; it never invents a hidden "Inbox Project", never auto-seeds a Project, and never makes the parent optional in UI while violating the spine. "Inbox" is the derived *planning* state of a parented task with no sector/schedule — not a parent.
  10. **Every bulk action is ONE atomic operation on the `TaskRepository` — including completion.** The `/tasks/bulk` route owns no mutation logic; it dispatches to a single repository method per intent (`setPriorityMany`, `setSectorMany`, `setCommitmentMany`, `setStatusMany`, `planTasks`/`clearPlans`, and **`completeTasks`**). Each method mirrors the ADR-030 §30.3 pattern: validate + resolve **every** id first (any missing/cross-workspace/archived id rejects the WHOLE operation before a single write), then contribute each changed task's own guarded statement group to ONE `D1Database.batch()`, so either all commit or none do; tasks already at the target value are counted `unchanged`. **Bulk completion is not a per-task loop** — `completeTasks` reuses the SAME atomic completion-and-clear-waiting group as `completeTask` (ADR-029 §29.4a; the shared spine completion builders stay the completion authority) for every open task in the selection, concatenated into a single transaction. A storage fault mid-batch therefore rolls the whole selection back — a subset of the selection can never be left completed while the operation reports failure. Proven by a real-D1 failure-path test that injects a forced fault into the bulk batch and asserts not one task in the selection is completed and no completion/waiting-clear Activity survives.
  11. **The Matrix and Sectors planning views scope to ACTIVE work only, server-side.** Both default to the `active` system view, whose predicate excludes every state that is not actionable *now*: completed, cancelled and Someday/Maybe (as the other execution views do) AND the two parked/blocked states — **waiting** (blocked on someone else) and **on_hold** (deliberately paused). So a completed/cancelled/deleted/waiting/someday/on-hold task never silently populates a quadrant or a sector bucket; those records stay reachable through **All Tasks**, the dedicated **Waiting**/**Someday**/**Completed**/**Cancelled** views, and the status filter. **`on_hold`'s treatment is explicit:** it is a real, retained workflow state that reads as "On hold" on every surface (the display-state evaluator), but it is *parked*, so it is shown only through All / its own status filter, never in the active planning buckets. The single `active` predicate is the source for both the `active` view clause and the grouping query, so they can never drift.
  12. **Matrix/Sectors grouping AND counts are server-authoritative — never derived from a globally-paginated page.** `listWorkspaceTaskGroups(dimension)` returns, in ONE bounded, N+1-free, workspace-scoped window-function query, each bucket's **authoritative total `count`** (computed over the whole active scope with `COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY bucket)`, independent of how many records were loaded) plus a bounded, deterministically-sorted top slice of that bucket (`ROW_NUMBER() OVER (…) ≤ bucketLimit`) and a `hasMore` flag. The loader feeds the Matrix (`quadrant`) and Sectors (`sector`) views from this grouping; the client renders accurate quadrant/sector counts and empty states before any paging, and a per-bucket **"View all N"** link to the equivalent filtered `all` view (which paginates that ONE bucket independently on its own scope-bound cursor) for an overflowing bucket. This removes the earlier client-side grouping of an accumulated global page (which made counts wrong and quadrants populate progressively). Mobile and desktop render the same loader grouping, so they always show the same population.
  13. **Task-parent search is a bounded, indexed query over the WHOLE collection.** `searchTaskParents(query)` runs a parameterised, workspace-scoped `LIKE` over `entities` restricted to active Areas + **non-archived** Projects, ordered deterministically (Projects first, then title, then id) and capped — never the DS-06 picker's fixed-prefix scan (which loaded only the first N entities and filtered in memory, so a newer Area/Project in a long-lived workspace could never be found). The `/tasks/parent-options` endpoint uses it; the create action still re-verifies the chosen parent, so this remains a selection convenience, never the authority.
  14. **The default `smart` sort is overdue-first against the owner's calendar day.** The `smart` order is one comparable keyset string: open-before-completed, then **overdue-before-not** (an OPEN task whose due date is strictly before the owner's `todayIso` — bound once via a `CROSS JOIN (SELECT ? AS today_iso)`, so due-today is *not* overdue), then priority P1→P4 (nulls last), then due date (nulls last). Because `todayIso` is already bound into the opaque pagination cursor's scope, a day change rejects a stale cursor rather than reinterpreting it. Proven by real-D1 tests (overdue P4 before non-overdue P1, multiple overdue, due-today, no-due, pagination across the overdue boundary, and cursor rejection on a day change).
  15. **Task creation is ONE atomic operation across the spine and the detail slice.** `TaskRepository.createTask(NewTaskInput)` writes the `entities` row (gated on an active, non-archived Area/Project parent), the `spine_records` row, the structural parent EntityLink, the `entity.created` + `entity_link.created` events AND the initial `task_details` planning slice (only when a planning field is supplied) in ONE `D1Database.batch()` — either everything commits or nothing does, so a task can never be left created-without-its-planning, half-linked or orphaned, and there is no spine-create-then-detail-write sequence to fail between. The identity/parentage SQL and event shapes are the SHARED spine create builders (extracted to `spine-database.ts` and reused by the SpineRepository itself), so the spine remains the identity authority and the parent-gate security SQL lives in ONE place. The `/tasks` quick-capture form posts to a dedicated **`/tasks/new` resource route** (no component) so the action's JSON is returned directly — a POST to the `/tasks` page route would render the document. Proven by real-D1 tests including a forced mid-batch fault that leaves no entity, detail row or Activity behind.
- **Consequences.** *Easy:* the owner plans the way they think (Matrix, Sectors, Someday, P1–P4 · Do/Defer/Delegate/Delete) over the exact same records Today executes and Projects organise; one display-state evaluator keeps every surface consistent; additive columns keep the migration low-risk; the read-model projection keeps workspace-wide views bounded and N+1-free without a second mutation path. *Hard:* the priority widening is a value-set change (a STRICT-table rebuild in migration `0012`) that ripples through validators, the Drawer and existing task tests; four independent axes are more model surface to keep coherent (mitigated by the single precedence evaluator and closed CHECK sets). *Accepted:* the delegatee is plain text until People exists (designed for a non-destructive upgrade); Time Sector membership is manual by design (no auto-promotion), trading convenience for the product's "never manufacture commitments" principle.
- **Alternatives considered.**
  - *One overloaded status enum (todo/in-progress/waiting/someday/planned/done/cancelled…).* Rejected — it collapses four orthogonal questions, duplicates completion/waiting/commitment that are already authoritative elsewhere, and guarantees contradictory states. The four-dimension split with a derived precedence is the whole point.
  - *A second "eisenhower_quadrant" column beside priority.* Rejected — priority already supplies the canonical dimension; two fields would drift. Widening the existing field to P1–P4 is the honest single source.
  - *Modelling Time Sector as a Project, tag or a second hierarchy.* Rejected — sector answers a different question (when) than Project (what); overloading Projects would corrupt parentage and rollups.
  - *Modelling Someday/Maybe as P4, On hold, a "someday" sector, or a fake Project/tag.* Rejected — commitment is orthogonal to priority, workflow and planning window; the smallest honest representation is its own two-value state.
  - *Auto-promoting sectors on calendar rollover (Next Week → This Week each Monday).* Rejected — it manufactures commitments the owner never made; promotion is offered in a review interaction, never automatic.
  - *A second workspace-wide task table/mutation repository for `/tasks`.* Rejected — it would fork the Task identity and mutation authority. The projection is read-only; the spine and `TaskRepository` remain the only writers.
  - *Loading the whole workspace into React to build Matrix quadrants / group sectors / sort / count.* Rejected — violates the bounded-read contract; all grouping, filtering, sorting, counting and overdue detection are server-authoritative and cursor-paginated.

## ADR-044: The writing-first live Markdown editor — adopting CodeMirror 6 as an authoring surface over the unchanged FND-08 source-and-render pipeline

- **Status:** Accepted.
- **Context.** NOTES-01B/01C/04 built the Note record on a plain Markdown `<textarea>` plus a desktop Source/Split/Preview view-mode toggle and a Notes-local formatting toolbar. That surface satisfied "author and store Markdown safely" but not the product goal ([NOTES-05](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-notes-05--writing-first-markdown-editor), studied against Apple Notes / Obsidian Live Preview / Notion): a single writing-first surface where the document is **styled as it is typed** (headings grow, emphasis/strikethrough/inline-code style, task items become checkboxes, thematic breaks and tables render) so a user writes naturally without remembering syntax — with no persistent preview/split mode. A `<textarea>` structurally cannot do this: all of its text is one uniform size and its markers cannot hide. The forces: (1) genuinely live, in-place rendering needs an editor that can vary line height and hide/replace ranges while keeping the caret correct — the industry-standard answer is CodeMirror 6 (what Obsidian itself uses); (2) DalyHub's [markdown strategy](../../AGENTS.md#97-markdown-strategy) is load-bearing — Markdown **source** is the single, durable, user-owned representation, rendered/sanitised through the ONE FND-08 pipeline with the ONE `MarkdownContent` HTML sink ([ADR-006](#adr-006-markdown-strategy)/[ADR-015](#adr-015-markdown-source-and-safe-rendering-pipeline)); (3) [`REFERENCE_PRODUCTS.md`](../reference/REFERENCE_PRODUCTS.md) previously recorded CodeMirror/ProseMirror/Tiptap as **not adopted**, "revisit only if a later Notes item genuinely needs rich authoring while still saving Markdown source" — NOTES-05 is exactly that item, so this is a fresh, deliberate evaluation, not a reversal by accident; (4) the [reuse policy](../../AGENTS.md#10-open-source-reuse-policy) explicitly names "editor" as a commodity to reuse rather than rebuild; and (5) the whole stack runs on Cloudflare Workers, so any new dependency must be SSR-safe.
- **Decision.**
  1. **Adopt CodeMirror 6 as an *authoring* surface only — never a render or storage foundation.** A new shared module `~/shared/markdown-editor` (`LiveMarkdownEditor`) hosts the one writing-first editor. The editor's **document IS the Markdown source string**, byte-for-byte; `onChange` always emits exactly that string. CodeMirror's Lezer Markdown grammar (`@codemirror/lang-markdown` + `@lezer/markdown` GFM) is used ONLY to produce a parse tree the editor styles the source from — it emits no HTML, never sanitises, and never becomes the stored representation. No rich-text/WYSIWYG document model, no proprietary JSON.
  2. **The FND-08 pipeline stays the sole renderer and sole sanitiser.** The editor adds **no second HTML sink**: inline constructs are styled with CSS classes on source ranges; the few block widgets (thematic rule, task checkbox, non-fetching image placeholder, rendered table) build DOM by hand with `document.createElement`/`textContent`, never an HTML-string sink — so `test/unit/markdown-boundary.test.ts`'s "one `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, in `MarkdownContent` only" invariant is untouched. The image widget honours the FND-08 remote-image policy (no `<img>`, no fetch); link *source* is edited but link resolution/URL policy stays in the pipeline. The unobtrusive **Read** mode renders the note through the exact FND-08 `renderMarkdownSource` → `<MarkdownContent>` path.
  3. **Live preview = decorate the source, reveal it on the caret.** A pure `buildLivePreviewDecorations(state)` walks the parse tree and returns line/mark/replace decorations; a construct shows its *rendered* form only while the selection is NOT inside it, and its raw Markdown returns the moment the caret enters — so editing is always over real source (this is Live Preview, not WYSIWYG). Block decorations (rule/table) are provided from a `StateField` (CodeMirror requires this); the builder is unit-tested directly against an `EditorState` with no browser.
  4. **Retire persistent Source/Split/Preview.** The primary interaction is the single live editor on every viewport (no wide-only Split to degrade); the only alternate is the unobtrusive Read toggle. The pure Markdown-source transforms and the formatting-action catalogue are **promoted unchanged** from the NOTES-04 Notes-local module to `~/shared/markdown-editor` (shared cannot depend on a module), and now back BOTH the toolbar and the keyboard shortcuts through one code path. Keyboard shortcuts are editor-scoped and never rebind the reserved global `Mod-K`/`/`.
  5. **The save/persistence contract is unchanged.** The editor is wired into the SAME DS-06 `useAutosaveField` coordinator, `SaveStatusIndicator`, offline detection, `UnsavedChangesGuard` and `suppressGuard`/flush behaviour NOTES-01C established; NOTES-05 changed the *authoring surface*, never the mutation path (`POST /notes/:noteId/mutate` `update_content`), the `note_details` storage, or the Activity model. No migration, no server change.
  6. **Progressive enhancement & SSR safety.** CodeMirror is imported lazily and constructed only in a client effect; the server (and any no-JS client, and non-layout test environments) renders an accessible, controlled `<textarea>` fallback with the same label/value/onChange, which the editor keeps in place if CodeMirror ever fails to load. The CM chunk is code-split and enters only the note-editor route.
  7. **Provenance recorded.** All added packages (`@codemirror/state|view|commands|language|lang-markdown`, `@lezer/markdown|highlight|common`) and their transitive `@codemirror/*`/`@lezer/*`/`crelt`/`style-mod`/`w3c-keyname` tree are MIT, pinned to exact versions, captured in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`, and the OSS reuse checklist is recorded in `REFERENCE_PRODUCTS.md`.
- **Consequences.** *Easy:* the note reads as formatted while it is typed (the headline product goal) with stable cursor/undo/IME/mobile behaviour inherited from a mature editor; one code path backs clicks and shortcuts; the source stays canonical and portable, so export (NOTES-06/X-04) is unaffected; the Diary body is a ready second consumer that can validate promoting the editor to the Design System. *Hard:* CodeMirror is the app's first substantial client dependency (~a few hundred KB, code-split and lazy-loaded on the editor route only); live-preview decoration logic is real surface to maintain; CodeMirror mounts only in a real browser, so its behaviour is proven by Playwright while the decoration/transform/table/command/view-mode logic is proven by pure unit tests. *Accepted:* the live table/rule/checkbox widgets are hand-built DOM (deliberately, to avoid a second HTML sink) and the live editor does not itself render nested inline Markdown inside table cells — the full FND-08 render is one Read toggle away; the decoration builder recomputes on each relevant transaction (fine within FND-08's 1 MiB bound and typical note sizes; the parse is incremental).
- **Alternatives considered.**
  - *Keep the textarea; ship only the roadmap-literal toolbar + reading mode.* Rejected — it cannot render "while editing"; a textarea's text is uniform, so headings can't grow and markers can't hide. It fails the stated NOTES-05 experience.
  - *A lightweight transparent-textarea-over-styled-mirror overlay (no dependency).* Rejected — it can colour/weight source but cannot vary font-size per line while keeping the caret aligned (the textarea's font-size is uniform), so headings can't genuinely enlarge. It also reimplements a fragile editor core (IME, selection, undo) that CodeMirror already solves.
  - *A WYSIWYG/rich-text editor (Tiptap/ProseMirror/Lexical) storing a document model.* Rejected — it makes an editor document (or proprietary JSON) the source of truth, violating the markdown strategy and portability; the task explicitly forbids WYSIWYG. CodeMirror keeps plain Markdown source as the document.
  - *Rendering live block widgets (tables/images) from the FND-08 pipeline's sanitised HTML via `innerHTML` inside a CM widget.* Rejected — it would create a second HTML-injection sink in spirit and defeat the one-sink invariant. Hand-built DOM from plain text is safe and sink-free.

## ADR-045: Today as the command centre — the personalisable widget landing surface over real cross-module reads

- **Status:** Accepted.
- **Context.** TODAY-01…06 built the calm daily home as a fixed set of sections: the real task planning bands + Waiting (TODAY-02/03/04), the real Active projects "Continue working" (PROJ-05 Slice 4), and **fixture-backed** calendar / recent-notes / daily-timeline sections plus an inert Quick Capture ([`TODAY_DASHBOARD.md`](../development/TODAY_DASHBOARD.md); the 2026-07 audit flagged this — UXA-12/13/20, [DEBT-31](../product/PRODUCT_DEBT.md)). [TODAY-08](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-today-08--today-as-the-command-centre) makes Today the product's **command centre**: the surface the owner spends most of their time on, where every important signal across the system surfaces intelligently without clutter — a *working* surface, explicitly **not** a chart dashboard ([PRODUCT_PRINCIPLES §4 "calm over urgent"](../product/PRODUCT_PRINCIPLES.md)). Forces: (1) the real read-models for the missing sections already exist and must be REUSED, not re-derived — the shared DS-05 workspace Activity Feed (`activity.listForWorkspace`), Notes (`entities.list({type:"note"})`), Diary (`DiaryRepository.list`), Areas (`AreaRepository.listAreas`), and Goals-with-alignment (`~/shared/alignment`); (2) the [module import boundary](../development/MODULES.md) forbids Today importing another module's internals — cross-module data flows only through the workspace-scoped repositories and the shared kernel; (3) an "information-dense but calm" surface needs **personalisation** (hide/move/pin/collapse, remembered) — a concept with no prior contract or ADR; (4) the whole surface must stay composed from the shared frame (ADR-020) with a correct single heading outline and WCAG 2.2 AA; (5) the existing TODAY-02…06 execution core (roving keyboard, contextual commands, swipe, bulk planning) must be preserved bit-for-bit.
- **Decision.**
  1. **Today is a personalisable set of widgets, composed in the ONE `CollectionLayout`.** A pure, React-free model (`app/modules/today/landing/layout.ts`) owns the widget catalogue and the state transitions (reorder / hide / pin / collapse) over a `TodayLayout`; `resolveVisibleWidgets` renders pinned-first, deterministically. The existing planning + Waiting execution core is preserved intact as the **"My day"** widget — its roving container, contextual commands, swipe tray and bulk bar are unchanged; only its section headings nest one level deeper (h2 widget → h3 section → h4 task card) to keep a correct outline.
  2. **The layout is a per-device UI preference, persisted client-side (localStorage), NOT workspace data.** A widget arrangement holds no entity content and is cosmetic, so it is deliberately not workspace/server-derived state — [ADR-016 §5.6](#adr-016-cloudflare-access-identity-app-shell-and-registry-driven-routing) keeps the *workspace* server-derived, and this preference is orthogonal to it. `useTodayLayout` is SSR-safe (server + first client render use the default; the snapshot applies in a post-mount effect, so no hydration mismatch), fails soft on disabled/quota'd storage, and normalises stale snapshots (unknown ids dropped, newly-shipped widgets appended) so a corrupt or outdated preference never breaks the surface.
  3. **Every data widget reads REAL workspace-scoped data; no fixtures, no re-derivation.** One bounded, independently-degrading loader (`app/modules/today/landing/load.ts`) reads Notes/Diary/Areas/Goals and derives the Morning Brief + Insights from the planning facts, reusing the SHARED pure evaluators (`evaluateGoalAlignment`, project `healthNeedsAttention`) — never a Today-only calculation. Each section catches independently, so one module failing blanks only that widget. The calendar / recent-notes / daily-timeline **fixtures are retired** (UXA-20/DEBT-31): the calendar becomes an honest placeholder in the Morning Brief, recent notes and the daily timeline become the real Notes widget and the real DS-05 Activity Feed.
  4. **Recent Activity is the first product consumer of the workspace-wide DS-05 Activity Feed.** A resource route `/today/activity` maps `activity.listForWorkspace(…)` through the shared `toActivityItems` (batched entity resolution, no N+1) against a **Today-owned descriptor map** that labels the cross-module event types by referencing only the KERNEL activity-type constants (`~/kernel/*`, shared — not module code), so the boundary holds; unknown types fall through to the shared safe generic fallback. The widget renders the shared `ActivityFeed` with the DS-07 `FilterBar` (event type / referenced entity / date, URL-bound), opening a referenced task in the SAME shared Task Drawer and other records at their canonical route.
  5. **Calm is enforced, not decorated.** No charts, no streaks, no red badges; Insights omit every zero-count signal (never "0 overdue"), frame accomplishments positively, and carry a quiet accent edge with a text label (never colour-only). Placeholders (weather, calendar, focus/deep-work/Pomodoro, natural-language capture) state honestly what will live there, matching the `ModuleComingSoon` honesty rule — they never fake data. Quick Capture stays the honest inert fixture until [TODAY-07](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-today-07--quick-capture-wiring) wires real creation.
- **Consequences.** *Easy:* Today now surfaces the whole system (tasks, activity, notes, diary, projects, areas, goals, insights) in one calm, remembered arrangement, and the execution core is untouched; connecting a future module is one widget + one loader read; the DS-05 feed proves the workspace-wide Activity path for later adopters (a Reviews digest, a Person timeline). *Hard:* one large `TodayDashboard` composition holds the widget switch (kept there deliberately so the TODAY-05 roving/command state stays in one component and never regresses); the loader fans out several bounded reads (parallelised, each degrading independently). *Accepted:* personalisation is per-device localStorage, not synced across devices (a deliberate first cut — a future workspace-preference sync can adopt the same pure model without changing widgets); at acceptance time Today's fixture-backed **search** provider was still deferred under DEBT-17, and X-01 later retired it entirely so Today now contributes no Search provider. The recent-notes widget reads the true newest notes through a dedicated `EntityRepository.listRecentByType` projection (newest-first, bounded — added with this item), never the oldest `entities.list` page re-sorted.
- **Alternatives considered.**
  - *Keep fixed sections; only wire the missing data.* Rejected — the brief and the "command centre" goal call for the owner to shape their own home; a fixed order cannot serve "spend most of their time here".
  - *Persist the layout as server/workspace state now.* Rejected for this slice — it is a cosmetic per-device preference with no entity content; forcing it into the server-derived workspace would over-couple a UI nicety to the security boundary. The pure model is storage-agnostic, so a later sync is additive.
  - *Build a bespoke dashboard-grid/drag-and-drop widget system.* Rejected — it invents a new visual language and a second layout engine against ADR-020's "compose, don't redesign". Widgets are ordinary labelled regions in the existing `CollectionLayout`; move/pin/hide are calm controls, and drag-reorder can adopt the existing shared reorder pattern later without a new system.
  - *Render Recent Activity from a Today-local event list.* Rejected — it would fork the single FND-05 Activity model (ADR-005/ADR-021). The workspace-wide `ActivityFeed` is the one renderer over the one stream.

## ADR-046: Area lifecycle — reversible archival on a module-owned slice, and the first guarded permanent-deletion purge with an audit tombstone

- **Status:** Accepted.
- **Context.** AREA-01 shipped the Areas module but explicitly deferred deletion, restoration, archival and a Settings surface ([`AREAS_MODULE.md` § Deferrals](../development/AREAS_MODULE.md)); the roadmap's lifecycle placeholder (PX-04) sketched only a reversible soft-delete/restore and "no permanent delete". [AREA-05](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-area-05--area-archive--safe-deletion-lifecycle) makes Area removal real and *safe*: the owner must be able to (a) archive an Area they are done with — reversibly, without touching its Goals/Projects/Tasks/Notes/Diary/links — and (b) permanently delete an Area, but only when it is genuinely empty, behind strict guards and an exact-title confirmation. Forces: (1) the FND-07 spine models only two lifecycle timestamps — `completedAt` (Areas never complete, by DB CHECK) and `deletedAt` (soft-delete) — and soft-delete is unsuitable for "archive" because it **blocks non-empty containers** (`SpineHasActiveChildrenError`) and makes the record **not-found by URL**, the opposite of what archive needs; (2) the spine principle ([ADR-014](#adr-014-spine-hierarchy-completion-and-rollup-semantics)) is that only the `SpineRepository` mutates spine identity/hierarchy, and there is deliberately **no hard deletion**; (3) every FK to `entities` is `ON DELETE RESTRICT`, and in particular `activity_subjects.entity_id` is RESTRICT precisely to preserve a deleted entity's Timeline — so a hard delete collides with an architectural **audit-retention** guarantee ([ADR-012](#adr-012-activity-persistence-and-atomic-mutation-recording)); (4) D1 has no cross-repository transaction, so any purge that spans identity + a module detail table must be one atomic batch; (5) the surface must reuse the shared DS-10b Settings/dangerous-action machinery and hold WCAG 2.2 AA.
- **Decision.**
  1. **Archival is a reversible state on a module-owned detail slice — the established `project_details`/`goal_details` precedent (ADR-037/ADR-039), NOT the spine and NOT hidden UI state.** A small `area_details` table (migration `0013_create_area_details.sql`) keyed by `(workspace_id, entity_id)`, pinned to the `area` entity type by a composite FK, holds ONE nullable `archived_at` and nothing the spine already owns. A new trusted `AreaSettingsRepository` (`archive`/`restore`) folds its precondition into one conditional write and appends `area.archived`/`area.restored` atomically via the shared `recordAtomicMutation` seam. Archiving is **always allowed on an active Area** (it preserves every descendant, link and Activity — it is not a delete and never cascades); restoring is always allowed. This is not a "second lifecycle model": it is the one archival model the codebase already uses, applied to Areas, because the spine deliberately does not model archival and its soft-delete cannot express "hidden-from-collection but readable, on a non-empty container".
  2. **The read projection makes archival visible without forking any model.** `AreaRepository.listAreas` excludes archived Areas (a `LEFT JOIN area_details … WHERE archived_at IS NULL`), the New-Project and New-Task parent pickers drop archived Areas via one bounded `listArchivedAreaIds`, and `getAreaOverview` keeps an archived Area **readable by its canonical URL** (it filters only soft-delete, never archival) and returns `archivedAt` so the record labels itself and guards Rename / New-Goal in the UI **and** server-side. A live `getAreaDependencySummary` counts the active links referencing the Area, grouped by kind, for the danger-zone blockers.
  3. **Permanent deletion is the SpineRepository's authority (`permanentlyDeleteArea`) — the only irreversible spine mutation — guarded and atomic.** It is workspace-scoped; refuses a non-Area id (`SpineWrongKindError`) and a missing/cross-workspace id (`SpineNotFoundError`); and is refused with `SpineHasDependentsError` whenever ANY active link still references the Area (child Goals/Projects/Tasks or a linked Note/Diary/other entity). The "genuinely empty" re-check is **folded into the mutating SQL and evaluated at commit**, so a dependent linked between page-load and submission still blocks the purge, and the batch is strictly all-or-nothing (every DELETE carries the same guard). When empty, one atomic `D1Database.batch()` deletes the Area's footprint in FK-safe order — `entity_links` → `activity_subjects` → `area_details` → `spine_records` → `entities` — so no `ON DELETE RESTRICT` FK is ever violated. Only Areas are permanently deletable in AREA-05 (they are the top of the spine and own no additive detail beyond `area_details`).
  4. **The audit-retention conflict is resolved by a purge-plus-tombstone, documented here rather than invented ad hoc.** Because `activity_subjects.entity_id` is RESTRICT, the entity cannot be removed while its Timeline subject rows point at it; and because the deletion event's own subject *would be* the vanishing row, the tombstone must be subject-less. So the purge removes the Area's `activity_subjects` associations (the append-only `activities` rows themselves are **retained** — ADR-012 — only their pointers to the deleted entity go, so no FK dangles and the workspace feed keeps its history) and appends ONE subject-less `area.deleted` Activity carrying the Area's id and title in its payload — the permanent, workspace-scoped audit record of the deletion, visible in the workspace Activity Feed and never on any entity Timeline (the entity is gone). No projection/materialised/cache rows exist to orphan (all module projections are read-only and derived).
  5. **The Settings tab composes the shared DS-10b system with the friction each action deserves.** `SettingsLayout` + `SettingsGroup tone="danger"` + `DangerousAction` + `ConfirmationDialog`, reusing the DS-03 focus/inert/scroll-lock hooks (no second focus trap). Reversible Archive/Restore uses no typed phrase; permanent Delete requires a **typed confirmation of the exact Area title** (case- and whitespace-significant), keeps Confirm disabled until it matches, and — when the Area is not empty — shows the grouped, linked dependency blockers with **no delete affordance at all** (no bypass, no force-delete). Deletion redirects to `/areas`; cancellation restores focus to the exact opener.
- **Consequences.** *Easy:* Areas gain a complete, safe lifecycle that reads as one system with Projects (same detail-slice archival shape, same danger-zone surface); the guarded-purge pattern (in-SQL commit-time re-check + FK-ordered atomic batch + subject-less audit tombstone) is now a documented template any future "permanent delete" can follow; archival is a single source of truth at the trusted boundary, never hidden client state. *Hard:* the SpineRepository's purge batch reaches the module-owned `area_details` table — a deliberate, minimal coupling justified by D1 having no cross-repository transaction; it is the entity-lifecycle authority clearing an entity's full footprint, documented at the call site. *Accepted:* the dependency guard blocks on **any** active link (including a soft-deleted/trashed child that retains its active structural parent link), so an Area whose child sits in the trash is not "empty" and cannot be permanently deleted until that child is restored-and-handled or the child itself gains a purge path (future work) — this is the safe direction (it never orphans a trashed child's rows). This ADR narrows AREA-01's deferral and extends PX-04's "no permanent delete" scope specifically for empty Areas; no `/trash` feature is introduced.
- **Alternatives considered.**
  - *Model archival as spine soft-delete (`deletedAt`).* Rejected — soft-delete blocks non-empty containers and returns not-found by URL, the opposite of archive's "hidden-from-collection but readable, on a lived-in Area", and repurposing it would break the established Deleted/All semantics.
  - *Add `archived_at` to `spine_records`.* Rejected for this item — it amends the sacred kernel schema and `SpineRecord` shape for a state only Areas use today, a broad blast radius against parallel work; the module-owned detail slice is the lower-risk, precedent-matching home, and the spine can adopt a first-class archival dimension later if more kinds need it.
  - *Keep the entity as a "tombstone" row instead of purging.* Rejected — it leaves a permanently soft-deleted shell and its detail/link/spine rows forever, contradicting the user's explicit "delete permanently" intent; the purge-plus-audit-event approach fully removes the Area while still satisfying the audit-trail guarantee through the retained workspace Activity fact.
  - *Cascade-delete descendants when deleting a non-empty Area.* Rejected outright — the product rule is never to silently cascade-delete user data; deletion is refused with grouped guidance until the Area is empty.
  - *Enforce deletion eligibility only in the UI / with a pre-read.* Rejected — the trusted server re-checks the same condition atomically in-SQL at commit, so the UI summary is advisory and a race can never delete a newly-non-empty Area.
- **Addendum (2026-08-05, AUDIT-FIX-03) — the template was adopted, not superseded.** Decision 4 called the purge-plus-subject-less-tombstone pattern "a documented template any future permanent delete can follow". The 5 August 2026 audit found that neither of the two other permanent-delete paths had actually followed it: the Asset purge wrote no tombstone at all [AUDIT-03 / DEBT-79], and the Review purge placed its Activity append before the deletes, carried an empty payload, deleted its own event's subject row and destroyed active links silently [AUDIT-04 / DEBT-80]. Both now follow this ADR unchanged — commit-time guard repeated on every destructive statement, FK-ordered child-first batch, retained `activities` rows, and ONE subject-less tombstone (`asset.deleted` with `{assetId, title}`, `review.deleted` with `{reviewId, title}`) inserted directly after the entity DELETE and guarded on its `changes()`. Two behaviours are recorded as deliberately *different in shape, identical in guarantee*: Assets and Reviews report a blocked purge as a typed **result** (`{ deleted: false, blockedReason: "has_links", linkCount }`) rather than the `SpineHasDependentsError` this ADR raises, and they report an already-gone record as an idempotent no-op rather than a not-found error. No decision here is amended or superseded; nothing about the Area path changed.

## ADR-047: The Universal Relationship System — one shared Linked Items surface, a generic /links endpoint, wiki links and linked-boosting

- **Status:** Accepted.
- **Context.** Relationships are a kernel primitive since FND-04 ([ADR-002](#adr-002-entitylinks)/[ADR-011](#adr-011-entitylink-persistence-and-lifecycle)), and DS-06 ([ADR-022](#adr-022-shared-forms--field-controls--declared-save-model-validation-boundary-and-the-entity-link-picker)) already shipped the entity-agnostic `EntityLinkPicker` and the trusted policy service (`createLinkWithPolicy`/`unlinkWithPolicy`/`searchLinkTargets`). But *using* relationships had drifted into bespoke, per-module surfaces — People and Meetings rendered a **read-only** linked list, Projects and Tasks each wired their own picker plus link-search/link-mutate routes — the exact shared-over-bespoke debt [`AGENTS.md §9.8`](../../AGENTS.md#98-shared-over-bespoke-and-one-authoritative-token-layer) forbids. The goal: every record's detail page gets ONE reusable **Linked Items** section (add existing, remove, search-as-you-type, navigate, hover-card summaries), links can be created from the Command Palette, Notes support inline `[[Wiki Links]]`, Search boosts a record's directly-linked entities, and Activity records relationship changes — all on the accepted primitives, with no second relationship model, table, or per-module link route. Forces: (1) the shared UI layer must not import the platform layer, but both must share the wire types; (2) the FND-08 Markdown pipeline is deliberately deterministic and stateless (no DB), so wiki-link *resolution* cannot happen in the renderer; (3) structural spine links (`*.belongs_to_*`) are reserved and already shown by the hierarchy, so a generic "everything linked" view must not duplicate or expose a back door around them; (4) global Search results carry provider-local item ids, not resolvable entity ids in general, so "boost linked entities" must be a safe, bounded lift rather than a cross-tier reordering; (5) the anchor entity id is client-supplied and therefore untrusted.
- **Decision.**
  1. **One module-agnostic relationship type, `link.related`, and a trusted universal policy.** `app/platform/entity-links/universal-links.ts` defines `link.related` (a validated FND-04 slug, not a reserved spine type), `buildUniversalLinkPolicy(anchorId)` (both directions, `link.related` only, many), `loadLinkedItems` (every active link at either end EXCLUDING the five reserved structural spine types, each flagged `removable` iff `link.related`) and `loadLinkSummary` (safe structural metadata only). Module-owned links (e.g. `meeting.attendee`) still appear in the view but read-only — only `link.related` is removable there.
  2. **One shared `/links` endpoint** (`app/routes/links.ts`), composed exactly like `/search` and `/commands` (renders no shell; `resolveAuthenticatedWorkspaceScope`; the client names only an anchor **entity** id). GET does list/search/summary; POST does policy-enforced link/unlink. It fails closed: a missing anchor → 404, a missing/invalid workspace → a calm unavailable, a crafted link id for a type/anchor the policy never offered → refused. No module needs its own link routes anymore.
  3. **One reusable Linked Items UI** (`app/shared/linked-items`): `LinkedItemsSection` (grouped-by-kind, each a navigable `EntityLink` inside a `HoverCard`, Remove for owned links, the DS-06 `EntityLinkPicker` — extended with a small `hideExistingList` prop — as the search-to-add affordance), `LinkedItemsTab` (the drop-in that also registers a `⌘K` **navigate** contextual action to the Linked tab), `HoverCard` (pointer+focus, `role="tooltip"` + `aria-describedby`, reduced-motion), and `useLinkedItems` (optimistic add/remove with rollback, offline-aware via the promoted shared `useOnlineStatus`, DS-10 Undo). Layering is respected: the wire types (`LinkedItem`/`LinkSummary`) live in the React-free shared model and the platform helper imports them from there (`platform → shared/*/model`, the same direction the DS-06 picker service already uses). `entityDestination` gains Meetings (`/meeting/:id`) so linked meetings navigate.
  4. **Wiki links resolve outside the renderer.** A pure remark transform (`app/platform/markdown/wikilinks.ts`) rewrites `[[Title]]`/`[[Title|Alias]]` into an ordinary internal link to `/notes/resolve?title=…` — deterministic, no DB lookup, no minted id, no second HTML sink, only a relative href the existing URL policy and strict sanitiser already permit (unstyled, to keep the allowlist intact). The one workspace-scoped step — title → record — happens at navigation time in the `/notes/resolve` route, which matches an active entity by title (notes preferred) and redirects to its canonical destination, landing on `/notes` rather than a dead end. `[[…]]` inside code or an existing link is never rewritten.
  5. **Linked-boosting is a safe in-tier lift.** `rankResults` accepts `boostIds`; a result whose provider-local item id is in the set is ordered above equally-relevant results **within the same relevance tier** — so a directly-linked record surfaces first but a boosted weak match never outranks a stronger tier. `/search` resolves the boost server-side from `?boostLinkedTo=<anchorId>` (the record's directly-linked ids); the client never supplies raw boost ids.
  6. **Activity is unchanged.** Relationship create/remove already append `entity_link.created`/`unlinked`/`restored` atomically with both endpoints as subjects; the shared DS-05 defaults render them on both records' Timelines and the workspace feed. No new Activity type.
- **Consequences.** *Easy:* every record type gains an identical, accessible Linked Items surface for one small tab entry; People/Meetings gain interactive linking they lacked; a new module gets relationships for free; the strict FND-08 safety envelope and the workspace-isolation boundary are untouched. *Hard:* two entity types (Diary, which opens in an Inspector rather than a Record-Layout tab; and the Projects/Tasks records that keep their existing picker tabs) are not yet migrated to the shared section — documented as follow-up, not regressions. *Accepted:* wiki links resolve by exact title (no fuzzy match, no disambiguation UI) and boosting is in-tier only — both deliberately conservative first cuts that the shared seams can deepen without a schema change.
- **Alternatives considered.**
  - *A per-module link table or bespoke tab per record.* Rejected — precisely the fragmentation ADR-002/011 and `AGENTS.md §9.8` forbid; the shared section + `/links` endpoint is the whole point.
  - *Resolve wiki links inside the Markdown renderer.* Rejected — it would make the FND-08 pipeline stateful (a DB lookup per render), breaking ADR-015 §4.7 determinism; resolution belongs at navigation time in a route.
  - *A styled `[[wikilink]]` class through the sanitiser.* Rejected for now — it would loosen the strict allowlist for cosmetics; a relative-href link is safe and sufficient.
  - *Boost linked entities across tiers (always on top).* Rejected — it would let a weak subtitle match on a linked record outrank an exact-title match elsewhere; the in-tier lift is the honest, bounded interpretation.
  - *Show structural spine links in the generic Linked Items view.* Rejected — the hierarchy already renders them, and making them removable there would bypass the SpineRepository's parentage authority (ADR-014); they are excluded from the view.

### §47.7 Review follow-up — corrective hardening (Codex review, PR #69, 2026-07-27)

A Codex review of the initial slice raised four P2 correctness gaps; all are fixed with focused regression tests, none needed a schema change or a new ADR (they harden the decisions above):

1. **The search boost is now reachable through the product UI.** §47 decision 5 wired the `/search` `boostLinkedTo` branch but no browser transport ever sent it, so boosting was dead code. `SearchSurface` now derives the record anchor from the current path (`app/shared/search/record-anchor.ts`, the inverse of the canonical record routes) and threads it through `useSearchController` → `fetchSearch`, which serialises `?boostLinkedTo=<anchorId>`. The client still only names the anchor record; the server resolves the boost set. Covered by `record-anchor.test.ts`, `client.test.ts` and a `useSearchController` propagation test.
2. **Boost IDs are matched in the providers' id namespace.** The boost set holds raw kernel entity ids, but `rankResults` compared them against provider-local `itemId`s, which repository-backed providers prefix (`person:<id>`, `task:<id>`, `meeting:<id>`) — so nothing ever matched. `SearchResultItem`/`TaggedResult` gained an optional canonical `entityId`; the entity-backed providers set it to the bare kernel id; `rankResults` boosts on `entityId ?? itemId`. Covered by rank + `validateResultItem` tests in `model.test.ts`.
3. **Linked Items paginate after structural-link filtering.** `loadLinkedItems` read only the first underlying link page and discarded `nextCursor`, then filtered reserved structural links from that already-truncated page — so an anchor with a page of structural links plus a later `link.related` link rendered empty. It now pages **through** the underlying pages while filtering, accumulates a display page, and returns a `nextCursor` whenever more remain; the `/links` `op=list` response, the client, the controller and the section (a shared `LoadMore`) carry pagination through. Covered by `test/unit/linked-items/universal-links.test.ts` and a `LinkedItemsSection` Load-more test.
4. **Wiki-link resolution has no correctness cutoff.** The resolver scanned only the first 5 entity pages (500 entities); a creation-ordered exact-title target beyond that wrongly fell back to `/notes`. It now pages through **all** cursor pages (stopping early on a note match). Covered by `test/kernel/notes-resolve-route.test.ts`, which seeds 501 entities with the target last and asserts it resolves.

## ADR-048: Meeting follow-through — Task-conversion orchestration and the source-item mapping

- **Status:** Accepted (MEET-02).
- **Context.** MEET-01 left agenda as free-form Markdown and decisions/outcomes as stable, ordered `meeting_items`, explicitly reserving Task conversion for MEET-02. Turning a meeting item into an actionable Task must: use the ONE canonical Task authority (no second Task model, status or priority vocabulary — [ADR-043](#adr-043--the-first-class-tasks-module-the-four-question-planning-model-time-sectors-somedaymaybe-and-derived-display-state)); make the Meeting↔Task relationship navigable from both ends through the Universal Relationship System ([ADR-047](#adr-047-the-universal-relationship-system--one-shared-linked-items-surface-a-generic-links-endpoint-wiki-links-and-linked-boosting)), not a bespoke layer; additionally record WHICH item produced the Task (a Meeting↔Task link alone cannot); prevent accidental duplicate conversion even across a partial failure; and never place private meeting content in Activity, telemetry or Task titles beyond the item text the owner chose to convert. Forces: (1) a Task structurally REQUIRES exactly one Area/Project parent, so conversion needs a parent selector, not a parentless task; (2) agenda is prose with no per-line identity, and parsing a relationship out of Markdown is forbidden ([AGENTS.md §9.7/§17]); (3) the FND-07 `createTask` encapsulates its OWN atomic `D1Database.batch()`, so the Task, the mapping, the link and the Activity cannot be fused into a single cross-repository transaction through the public contracts.
- **Decision.**
  1. **Agenda gains stable structured identity.** Migration `0015` widens the `meeting_items.kind` CHECK to admit `agenda` alongside `decision`/`outcome` (a STRICT-table rebuild preserving every row), so an agenda item is convertible with the same stable id — never by parsing `agenda_markdown`, which is retained unchanged as the agenda narrative.
  2. **A narrow, durable source-item mapping supplements — never replaces — the EntityLink.** `meeting_item_tasks(workspace_id, meeting_id, item_id, task_id, created_at)` (migration `0015`): `PRIMARY KEY (workspace_id, task_id)` (one Meeting source per Task); a partial unique index on `(workspace_id, item_id) WHERE item_id IS NOT NULL` (at most one converted Task per source item; direct follow-ups have `item_id NULL` and are exempt); `FOREIGN KEY (workspace_id, meeting_id) → meeting_details ON DELETE CASCADE` (a deleted Meeting drops its mapping rows but never the Tasks). Workspace-scoped, parameterised, no client-supplied workspace/actor. Identity is the stable item id, so a mapping survives item reordering. The navigable relationship stays a `task.relates_to` EntityLink (source Task → target Meeting), which surfaces the Meeting in the Task Drawer's Linked section AND the Task (read-only) in the Meeting's universal Linked Items — one row, navigable both ways.
  3. **An explicit orchestration owns the multi-write conversion** (`app/platform/meetings/follow-up-operations.ts` — it lived in `app/modules/meetings/` until [§73.1](#731-addendum--the-acceptance-path-canonical-conversion-authority-proposed-notes-and-openai-application-state-storage-ai-02-2026-08-05) re-homed it so the AI acceptance path could use the SAME authority without breaching the module-boundary rule; nothing about the orchestration changed). Every Task field flows through `scope.tasks.createTask`/`updateTask` (the Task authority; the Meeting module writes no Task rows). The **commit point** is `meetings.linkFollowUpTask`, which writes the mapping row AND the structural Activity (`meeting.item_converted_to_task` / `meeting.follow_up_created`, both with the Meeting and Task as subjects, payload = item kind only) in ONE batch. **Idempotency** is item-keyed: a repeat conversion returns the same Task and re-asserts the idempotent `task.relates_to` link. **Duplicate rejection & recovery**: a concurrent winner trips the partial unique index (`MeetingFollowUpConflictError`); the just-created duplicate Task is compensated (soft-deleted through the spine) and the winner returned. Any other pre-commit failure soft-deletes the created Task, so a reported failure is truthful and a retry is clean. A converted Task later deleted clears its stale mapping and the item is convertible again.
  4. **Structural Activity only, and the People seam is the existing link event.** The two new activity types carry only the item kind. Attendee `meeting.attendee` links surface on a Person's Timeline through the kernel's both-endpoints `entity_link.created`; meaning-specific People-timeline events are deferred to MEET-03/PEOPLE-02 rather than inventing a People-specific history model.
- **Consequences.** *Easy:* a meeting becomes an actionable follow-through surface reusing the canonical Task Drawer, Task planning, the Universal Relationship System and the shared Activity/Timeline; per-item conversion state and duplicate prevention are exact; archived meetings are read-only while their Tasks stay navigable; meeting deletion never cascade-deletes Tasks. *Hard / accepted residual:* because `createTask` encapsulates its own batch, a hard process crash in the gap between `createTask` committing and the mapping committing can leave one Task with no mapping — invisible to the mapping-backed Follow-up surface, so a retry could create a second Task. A single fused batch would remove this; it is documented and accepted rather than hidden, with idempotency covering every non-crash retry. The orchestration and all partial-failure points are covered by kernel/D1 tests.
- **Alternatives considered.**
  - *Encode the source item in the `task.relates_to` link or in Markdown.* Rejected — a link cannot say which item, and parsing prose for a relationship is forbidden; the narrow mapping table is the smallest durable seam.
  - *A Meeting-local task list/table.* Rejected — it would fork the Task model; the Follow-up tab queries canonical Tasks and groups them via the shared `taskDisplayState`.
  - *Refactor `createTask` to expose its statements so the whole conversion is one batch.* Rejected for MEET-02 — it would leak D1 statements across the kernel Task contract; the documented orchestration with a commit point + idempotency + compensation is the sanctioned boundary.
  - *A dedicated `meeting.produced_task` link type.* Rejected as the navigational link — it would NOT appear in the Task Drawer's `task.relates_to`-filtered Linked section, failing bidirectional navigation; `task.relates_to` (the canonical user relation) satisfies requirement 5 while the mapping carries provenance.

---

## ADR-049: First-class Assets — the `asset_details` slice, integer minor-unit money, and the real-world-status-vs-record-archive split

- **Status:** Accepted (ASSET-01).
- **Context.** DalyHub needs to track things of value — physical (vehicles, appliances, tools), digital (software, subscriptions) and documentary/financial (licences, insurance policies, warranties) — as first-class records that link across the spine, without depending on external file storage, OCR, barcode scanning, AI or reminders (all out of scope for the first version). Two forces are new to the codebase: (1) an Asset carries **money** (purchase price, replacement value), and DalyHub had no monetary representation before this; a floating-point amount silently loses precision, which is unacceptable for a value store. (2) An Asset has a **real-world lifecycle** (Active / Stored / Loaned / Under repair / Retired / Disposed) that is genuinely independent of whether the DalyHub RECORD is archived — a disposed vehicle can remain an active record you keep for history, and an archived record can still be "Active" in the world. Assets must reuse every existing seam (the generic entity layer, EntityLinks/Universal Relationship System, the shared Activity stream, Record/Collection Layout, forms, search, commands, subtype icons) and add no second generic entity system, relationship table, Activity stream or file-storage provider.
- **Decision.**
  1. **Assets are ordinary `asset` entities plus one additive STRICT `asset_details` slice** (migration `0016`), following the People/Diary supporting-entity pattern exactly. Identity, title and soft-delete/restore stay `entities.*`; the structured Asset fields (type, status, identity, ownership/location as canonical ids, acquisition & value, warranty & service, document/policy/licence) live in `asset_details`, keyed by `(workspace_id, entity_id)` with a composite FK to `entities(workspace_id, id, type)` and `ON DELETE RESTRICT`. The `asset` type is **reserved**: the generic EntityRepository refuses to CREATE one, so an Asset can never exist without its detail row; only the authoritative workspace-bound `AssetRepository` creates one, atomically with its `asset.created` event. Ownership/location references (owner Person, responsible Person, Area) are stored as **canonical ids**, never duplicated records, and relationships across the spine stay FND-04 EntityLinks (`asset` is added to the Universal Relationship System's supported endpoints and to the shared entity-destination map).
  2. **Money is integer minor units + an ISO-4217 currency code, never a float** (`app/kernel/money`). A new dependency-light money helper parses a human decimal string into integer minor units using string arithmetic (no float multiplication), formats/round-trips exactly, resolves a currency's minor-digit count from `Intl`, and performs NO currency conversion (explicitly out of scope). The two amount columns are `INTEGER` with a non-negative CHECK. This is the first money representation in the codebase, so it carries this ADR.
  3. **Real-world status and record archive are two independent lifecycles, documented as such.** `asset_details.status` (a small stable vocabulary) describes the Asset in the world and is edited through the Details form (a status change appends `asset.status_changed`, or `asset.disposed` when moving to disposed). `asset_details.archived_at` (reversible put-away, mirroring People/Projects) controls whether the record appears in active collections and is toggled through Settings (`asset.archived`/`asset.restored`). Neither touches the other; both are distinct again from `entities.deleted_at` soft-deletion.
  4. **Dates are wall-calendar `YYYY-MM-DD` strings compared as integers in the owner timezone** (ADR-022 §22.7). One canonical date-status evaluator (`app/modules/assets/asset-dates.ts`) classifies every due date (overdue / due-soon / today / future / historical) and picks the single "next meaningful date"; the collection card, Summary and Dates tab all derive from it — due-date logic is never duplicated. The `expiring` and `service_due` collection views bound their SQL by an owner-calendar horizon computed from the repository clock.
  5. **Sensitive values never leave the record.** Serial/reference numbers, prices and private notes are marked private; the collection card projection omits them entirely, search matches and snippets exclude them, and Activity payloads carry only changed field NAMES and the (non-sensitive) status vocabulary term — never a value (AGENTS.md §5/§17).
  6. **Permanent deletion is guarded.** `AssetRepository.permanentlyDelete` refuses while any ACTIVE relationship references the Asset (so linked Notes/Tasks/People are never silently orphaned); once unlinked it purges the Asset's footprint (historical links, activity subjects, detail row, entity) child-first in one atomic batch carrying a "no active link" guard that closes the read→submit race. It never touches a linked record.
- **Consequences.** *Easy:* Assets get the full product surface (collection with views/filters/sort/cursor pagination, canonical record, progressive create, Linked Items, Timeline, search, commands, subtype icons) by reusing shared seams with zero central-switch edits; the money helper and date evaluator are reusable by future modules; the two-lifecycle split is explicit rather than conflated. *Hard / accepted:* the collection loads bounded People/Area candidate lists (limit 100) to populate filter and picker selects, so a workspace with hundreds of People shows a bounded set — acceptable for the first version and replaceable with an async picker later; owner/responsible/area are structured id fields AND linkable relationships, a deliberate small redundancy that makes them filterable. *Deferred (product debt, no dead UI):* real file attachments, R2/object storage, OCR, barcode/QR scanning, recurring reminders and automated warranty alerts, service-history logbooks, depreciation/tax, receipt/email ingestion, external subscription sync, AI extraction, and household sharing beyond current workspace rules.
- **Alternatives considered.**
  - *Store money as a float or a decimal-in-text.* Rejected — floats lose precision; a text decimal defers the same parsing problem to every read. Integer minor units + a currency code is exact and index-friendly.
  - *Model real-world status as the record archive state.* Rejected — they are genuinely independent (a disposed asset can stay an active record; an archived record can be "Active"); conflating them would lose real information.
  - *A second entity/relationship system or a per-type Asset table.* Rejected — precisely the fragmentation `AGENTS.md §9.8` forbids; one additive slice + EntityLinks + one form architecture covers every subtype through type-driven progressive disclosure.
  - *Separate create forms per subtype.* Rejected — a single progressive form reveals only type-relevant fields and preserves entered common values when the type changes; the record's Details tab always edits the full slice.
